questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, the only problem was that many locals didn't speak english. It was fine at restaurants and bars, but don't expect a lot of help in the grocery stores.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sadly we didn't meet many.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language barrier.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Many had a quite good humor. We went to a lot of comedy shows.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I) Socialize all you can, there are hundreds of exchange students II) Travel in the weekends and holidays and see more of Eastern Europe III) Enjoy Budapest as the great city it is - it never sleeps.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Before leaving I was a bit afraid that Budapest was more of a weekend get-away city. I didn't get tired of it at all though. 
It is a great city with a lot to do and it is also cheap, which makes it a bit more fun to be an exchange student. Even though it might be a little uncommon to go to Budapest/Hungary from Denmark, it is a very popular destination from other countries. I think we were close to a thousand exchange students that semester, even with covid and everything. I only spent time with people from other nationalities, which I think is also the point of going on exchange - and I made some very close and good friends. 
Furthermore, we rarely ate at home, because food and drinks are very cheap. But you still have to save up, because you spent more than you think. 
Regarding the university, I liked the campus and the extra activities. The academic level in the exams was not very difficult, but I still feel like I learned a lot through the semester, without being slammed with "homework". 
All together I felt it was a great place to be an exchange student.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the experiences and getting some new relations. It is good to get a break from your everyday life in DK.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The war in Ukraine, which made our situation a bit unsure in the beginning, since we all of a sudden were quite close. But I also think it was important to see what was happening, and how many of the locals in Budapest that did everything they could to help the refugees. You are in your own bubble on your exchange, but there is still and outside world, which we were reminded. We met quite many citizens from Ukraine, and I think it was an important experience to meet and talk with them as well. Besides from that, the city didn't change much during our stay, and a lot of turist were still visiting.

questions.answer: Yes
